Subject: Post-call: SDK/Auth/Routing + Observability trace plan

Thanks for taking the time today — quick recap from our discovery call and clear next steps so we all stay aligned. TL;DR: FinLytics will pilot Redwood for an insights reranking workflow (embedding + reranker) and needs SDK samples, an auth pattern for ephemeral keys, routing rules for latency-sensitive queries, and observability hooks (trace IDs, latency breakdown headers, and a basic dashboard).

Summary of decisions
- Pilot scope: embeddings + reranker for search relevancy (query volume ~5k/day, 99th pct latency target 300ms).
- Deployment preference: start with Redwood Hosted API; evaluate Dedicated if unit costs require.
- Observability: must include per-request trace-id propagation, tokenized latency breakdown headers, and an ops dashboard with token/latency cost slices.

Open technical questions (assigned)
- Auth: do you want short-lived client-side tokens (recommended) or server-side only (Maya to confirm) — ACTION Maya
- Routing: define which traffic needs low latency vs batch (Theo to provide traffic mix) — ACTION Theo
- Embedding model constraints: desired vector size and similarity thresholds — ACTION FinLytics

Next steps / owners
- Monica: deliver SDK quickstart repo + auth sample (server token exchange + client ephemeral) by 2026-10-05. (attachment: redwood-sdk-quickstart.zip)
- Theo/Maya: share a one-page architecture sketch and expected traffic profile by 2026-10-02. (attachment: finlytics-arch-v1.pdf noted)
- Karthik: schedule follow-up technical sync the week of 2026-10-05 and create HubSpot milestone.

Observability specifics requested by FinLytics (not exhaustive)
- Trace propagation: support custom inbound header (X-Client-Trace or X-B3-TraceId) and Redwood echoing back trace-id in responses.
- Latency headers: per-request header with breakdown (eg: X-Redwood-Latency: compile=10ms;kv-cache=5ms;gen=180ms) for easier SLO dashboards.
- Logging fields: request_id, trace_id, model_variant, seq_len, tokens_in, tokens_out, cost_usd.
- Dashboard: prebuilt Grafana dashboard with percentile latency, token cost over time, per-model throughput.

If anything above is off, flag it here. Otherwise Monica will post the SDK repo and a short auth flow doc by Monday.

Thanks,
Karthik

Thanks Karthik — useful recap. A few clarifications from our side: 

1) Auth: we prefer server-side token exchange + short-lived client tokens for browser-based UIs (we can implement a token mint endpoint).
2) Traffic mix: roughly 70% background batch embeddings (off-peak latency ok), 30% interactive rerank requests with strict p99 targets. We'll send a CSV with hourly qps.
3) PII concerns: some user text includes masked PII; we need to confirm data residency — happy to start hosted for dev but may require Dedicated or Private for production.

Attaching a very rough architecture sketch (finlytics-arch-v1.pdf). Our immediate priority is the interactive reranker observability so support can quickly debug latency spikes.

We'll aim to get the traffic profile to you by EOD 2026-10-02. Thanks for the Monica follow-up.

Subject: SDK quickstart + concrete observability hooks (sample code & headers)

Hi team — attaching the SDK quickstart and dropping concrete examples here so you can prototype quickly. I've included both Node and Python snippets and an example of the headers/payloads we'll echo.

Auth pattern (recommended)
1) Client hits your backend: /mint-redwood-token -> backend exchanges server key for short-lived ephemeral token (10m).
2) Client uses ephemeral token for direct calls to Redwood API.

Node fetch example (ephemeral token):
fetch('https://api.redwood.com/v1/generate', {
  method: 'POST',
  headers: {
    'Authorization': 'Bearer <EPHEMERAL_TOKEN>',
    'X-Client-Trace': '<uuid-v4>',
    'Content-Type': 'application/json'
  },
  body: JSON.stringify({ model: 'rw-embed-compact-3', input: '...' })
})

Observability headers we will support/echo:
- Accepts: X-Client-Trace (prefer this if you already propagate a trace id)
- Returns: X-Redwood-Trace: <trace-id>
- Returns: X-Redwood-Latency: compile=12ms;kv=4ms;gen=220ms;network=6ms
- Returns: X-Redwood-Model: rw-ranker-v2

Logging fields we add to request logs (searchable in our console/exportable to your SIEM): request_id, trace_id, client_id, model, seq_len, tokens_in, tokens_out, cost_usd, route_variant

Structured output / tool calling note
- For reranking, consider returning a structured JSON array of {id, score, reasoning} so your service can apply business rules client-side. Example: {"id":"doc_123","score":0.87,"explanation":"matched key phrase 'quarterly revenue'"}

Embeddings + reranker guidance
- Use rw-embed-compact-3 for storage (vector size 768).
- For reranker, we recommend a two-stage pipeline: ANN candidate generation -> rw-ranker-v2 for top-20 reordering. Set similarity cutoff 0.72 as a starting point.

Dashboards & alerts
- We pushed a Grafana import (link below) with panels for p50/p95/p99 latency per model, token spend per route, and a heatmap of latency sources (compile/kv/gen).
- Suggested alerts: p99 > 300ms sustained 5m, token burn increase >30% week-over-week.

Deliverables I will share by EOD: SDK quickstart repo link, ephemeral auth snippet, Grafana dashboard export.

If you want, we can do a short 30-minute runbook workshop during the technical sync so your SREs can validate trace propagation end-to-end.

Cheers,
Monica Patel
